definitions.explanation: The design and arrangement of dance movements and sequences for a performance. Also refers to the movements themselves once arranged.

examples.japanese: {振|ふ}り{付|つ}け⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{覚|おぼ}える→覚える：00739_oboeru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{苦労|くろう}した→苦労する：25357_kurousuru⟧。
examples.english: I struggled to learn the choreography.

examples.japanese: ⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧な{振|ふ}り{付|つ}け{師|し}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{舞台|ぶたい}→舞台：03606_butai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{担当|たんとう}→担当：02567_tantou⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: A famous choreographer was in charge of this stage production.

examples.japanese: ⟦ダンス→ダンス：03856_dansu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{振|ふ}り{付|つ}け⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{動画|どうが}→動画：04443_douga⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{確認|かくにん}→確認：00158_kakunin⟧し⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧⟦{練習|れんしゅう}している→練習する：22991_renshuusuru⟧。
examples.english: I'm practicing while checking the dance choreography on video.

notes:
USAGE:
Derived from the verb {振|ふ}り{付|つ}ける (to choreograph). Used in dance, theater, musicals, and idol/pop performance contexts. The person who creates choreography is called a {振|ふ}り{付|つ}け{師|し} (choreographer).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {振|ふ}り{付|つ}け⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{覚|おぼ}える→覚える：00739_oboeru⟧: to learn choreography
- {振|ふ}り{付|つ}け⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{考|かんが}える→考える：00856_kangaeru⟧: to create/devise choreography
- {振|ふ}り{付|つ}け{師|し}: choreographer

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{踊|おど}り→踊り：01347_odori⟧: dance (the dance itself, not the arrangement)
- コレオグラフィー: choreography (loanword, less common in everyday speech)
